study_identification_part.si_4_title: Nomograms of human hippocampal volume shifted by polygenic scores

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: UK Biobank (UKB) was used as the primary dataset to construct the normative models (GPR and SWA nomograms). The Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) was used as an application dataset to evaluate the clinical impact of the nomograms on dementia patients.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: Using imaging data from 35,686 healthy subjects aged 44-82 from the UK Biobank (UKB), we built HV nomograms using Gaussian process regression (GPR)... Clinical impact of genetically adjusted nomograms was investigated by comparing 818 subjects from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database...

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: UK Biobank (N=35,686) was used to train and construct the normative models (both SWA and GPR). ADNI (N=818) was used for external evaluation and to test the clinical utility of the genetically adjusted nomograms in differentiating CN, MCI, and AD patients.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Using 35,686 subjects from the UK Biobank, we generate nomograms using two methods: a previously reported sliding window method (SWM) and Gaussian process regression (GPR)... Clinical impact of genetically adjusted nomograms was investigated by comparing 818 subjects from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database...

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Both the primary Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) model and the baseline Sliding Window Approach (SWA) were developed using the same cohort of 35,686 healthy subjects from the UK Biobank.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: Using 35,686 subjects from the UK Biobank, we generate nomograms using two methods: a previously reported sliding window method (SWM) and Gaussian process regression (GPR).

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The healthy subjects from the UK Biobank used for both GPR and SWA models were in the age range of 44-82 years. Detailed descriptive statistics (mean, SD, median) for the final sample of 35,686 subjects were not explicitly provided in the text or supplementary tables.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: While the paper notes that the initial UK Biobank pool consisted of 39,664 subjects including 18,718 females (47.2%), it does not specify the exact sex distribution for the final analytic sample of 35,686 subjects used to build the normative models.
